target.title: fix(validation): automerge repair rejects valid pnpm lockfiles
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108974

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClawSweeper automerge repairs would stop before validation when a valid pnpm lockfile integrity value contained double slashes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dependency-install guard now recognizes protocol-relative URLs only when they begin at a URL boundary. This retains the fail-closed network policy for actual install destinations while avoiding false positives from opaque SHA-512 integrity data.

## User Impact

Operators can rerun affected automerge repairs without valid pnpm lockfiles being rejected as unapproved external dependency hosts. Actual non-registry install URLs remain blocked.

## Evidence

- `pnpm run build` and `pnpm run build:repair` passed.
- Focused regression test passed: `dependency setup permits pnpm integrity strings containing double slashes`.
- Focused network-policy test passed, including a semicolon-prefixed external URL in `bun.lock` that remains rejected.
- Explicit `https://` URLs remain detectable after a non-boundary character, while only bare protocol-relative `//` tokens require a boundary.
- The regression fixture uses the integrity shape that blocked the OpenClaw repair worker.
- Real-target preflight against the exact head of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108974 reached Corepack preparation without the former unapproved-destination error. The local install then stopped on an independent Corepack request for `https://registry.npmjs.org//pnpm/11.2.2`; this is not presented as a completed repair-worker run.

target.title: Consolidate automerge worker health
target.body:
## What changed

- removed the standalone Automerge Reliability sidebar panel
- consolidated automerge repair workflow activity, stalls, failures, recoveries, and unresolved failures into Worker Health
- kept PR and workflow run links while moving average runtime into secondary detail
- labeled the data as Automerge worker operations so it is not confused with Automerge Product Health success metrics

## Why

Automerge repair workflow reliability is an operational worker signal. Presenting it as a peer panel beside Worker Health made it too easy to confuse workflow failures with the separate product-level automerge success rate.

The workflow collection, cache, API payload, and hero attention signal remain unchanged.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build:dashboard`
- `node --test test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` (136 passed)
- `pnpm run check`
- autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.93)
